entries.title: Zionism
entries.text: Movement for the Jewish return to the land of Israel and national renewal there. Herzl gave it a political form in 1897.

entries.title: Abraham Accords
entries.text: Normalization agreements signed in 2020 between Israel and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, followed by Morocco and Sudan. They were brokered by the United States.

entries.title: Balfour Declaration
entries.text: Letter of 2 November 1917 in which the British government expressed support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.

entries.title: Six-Day War
entries.text: War of June 1967 in which Israel took the Sinai, Gaza, the Golan Heights, Judea and Samaria and East Jerusalem.

entries.title: Yom Kippur War
entries.text: War of October 1973 in which Egypt and Syria attacked Israel on the holiest day of the Jewish year. Israel recovered and crossed the Suez Canal.

entries.title: War of Independence
entries.text: War from 1947 to 1949 that followed the UN Partition Plan and Israel's declaration of independence on 14 May 1948.

entries.title: Oslo Accords
entries.text: Agreements of 1993 and 1995 between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization that set up the Palestinian Authority.

entries.title: Camp David Accords
entries.text: Framework agreements signed in 1978 by Menachem Begin and Egypt's Anwar Sadat that led to the 1979 peace treaty and Israel's return of the Sinai.

entries.title: Iron Dome
entries.text: Israeli air-defense system in use since 2011 that intercepts short-range rockets and shells. It was developed by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems.

entries.title: Hamas
entries.text: Palestinian Islamist movement founded in 1987 that has ruled Gaza since 2007. Israel, the United States and the European Union list it as a terrorist organization. It led the October 7, 2023 attack.

entries.title: Hezbollah
entries.text: Lebanese Shia militia and political party formed in 1982 with Iranian support. It fought Israel in the Second Lebanon War.

entries.title: October 7 attack (2023)
entries.text: Attack by Hamas on southern Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and about 250 taken hostage. It began the war in Gaza.

entries.title: Gaza
entries.text: Ancient coastal city and Philistine center on the Mediterranean, today the Gaza Strip.

entries.title: Golan Heights
entries.text: Basalt plateau between the Galilee and Syria. Israel took it in the Six-Day War and applied its law there in 1981.

entries.title: Jerusalem
entries.text: Capital of Israel and the holiest city of Judaism. King David made it his capital about 1000 BCE and Solomon built the First Temple there. Rebuilt after the Babylonian exile and destroyed again by Rome in 70 CE, it passed through many hands before the Six-Day War of 1967 reunited it under Israeli control.

entries.title: Old City of Jerusalem
entries.text: Walled area of about one square kilometer, with the Jewish, Christian, Muslim and Armenian quarters. It holds the Temple Mount, the Western Wall and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

entries.title: Western Wall
entries.text: Retaining wall of the Temple Mount platform from the time of Herod. It is the holiest place where Jews may pray and is also called the Kotel.

entries.title: Temple Mount
entries.text: Platform in the Old City of Jerusalem where the First Temple and Second Templestood. It is the holiest site in Judaism. Today the Dome of the Rock and the Al- Aqsa Mosque stand on it, and Muslims count it their third holiest site.

entries.title: Dome of the Rock
entries.text: Shrine with a golden dome on the Temple Mount, completed in 691 CE by the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik. It is the oldest surviving major work of Islamic architecture.

entries.title: Masada
entries.text: Mountain fortress above the Dead Sea built by Herod. It was the last stronghold of the Jewish revolt against Rome and fell in 73 or 74 CE.

entries.title: Dead Sea Scrolls
entries.text: About 900 manuscripts found in caves near Qumran, written from the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE. They include the oldest known copies of books of the Hebrew Bible.

entries.title: Dead Sea
entries.text: Salt lake between Israel and Jordan, about 430 meters below sea level, the lowest land on earth. Its level is falling by about a meter a year.

entries.title: Tel Aviv
entries.text: City founded in 1909 on sand dunes north of Jaffa. Its Bauhaus- style White City was named a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2003.

entries.title: Haifa
entries.text: Israel's third largest city, on the slopes of Mount Carmel. It has a major port, the Technion and the Bahai Gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

entries.title: Law of Return
entries.text: Law of 1950 that gives every Jew the right to immigrate to Israel and become a citizen. A 1970 amendment extended it to relatives.

entries.title: Aliyah
entries.text: Immigration of Jews to the land of Israel, from the Hebrew word for "ascent." Historians count successive waves from 1882, starting with the First Aliyah.

entries.title: Theodor Herzl
entries.text: Viennese journalist, 1860 to 1904, founder of political Zionism. He convened the First Zionist Congress at Basel in 1897.

entries.title: David Ben-Gurion
entries.text: Leader of the Jewish community before independence, who declared the state on 14 May 1948 and was Israel's first prime minister. He retired to Sde Boker in the Negev.

entries.title: Golda Meir
entries.text: Israeli prime minister from 1969 to 1974. Born in Kyiv in 1898 and raised in Milwaukee, she was foreign minister before she led the country through the Yom Kippur War and resigned the following year.

entries.title: Menachem Begin
entries.text: Israeli prime minister from 1977 to 1983 and former head of the Irgun. He signed the Camp David Accords with Egypt.

entries.title: Yitzhak Rabin
entries.text: Israeli general and prime minister who signed the Oslo Accords. A Jewish extremist assassinated him in Tel Aviv on 4 November 1995.

entries.title: Shimon Peres
entries.text: Israeli statesman, 1923 to 2016, who served as prime minister, foreign minister and ninth president. He shared the 1994 Nobel Prize for peace with Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat for the Oslo Accords.

entries.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
entries.text: Israeli prime minister, first elected in 1996 and the longest serving in the country's history. He leads the Likud party.

entries.title: Ariel Sharon
entries.text: Israeli general and prime minister from 2001 to 2006. He carried out the Disengagement from Gaza in 2005, and a stroke in January 2006 ended his career. He died in 2014.

entries.title: Entebbe raid
entries.text: Israeli commando operation of 4 July 1976 that freed hostages held by hijackers at Entebbe Airport in Uganda. The unit's commander, Yonatan Netanyahu, was killed.

entries.title: Operation Protective Edge
entries.text: Seven-week Israeli campaign in Gaza in July and August 2014, in response to rocket fire and tunnel attacks.

entries.title: Second Intifada
entries.text: Palestinian uprising that began in September 2000 and brought a wave of suicide bombings. It lasted until about 2005.

entries.title: UN Partition Plan
entries.text: United Nations resolution of 29 November 1947 proposing a Jewish and an Arab state with Jerusalem under international rule. The Jewish leadership accepted it and the Arab states rejected it.

entries.title: British Mandate
entries.text: British rule over the land, assigned by the League of Nations and lasting from the 1920s until May 1948.

entries.title: Holocaust
entries.text: Nazi Germany's murder of six million Jews in Europe from 1941 to 1945. Israel marks it each year on Yom HaShoah.

entries.title: Yad Vashem
entries.text: Israel's Holocaust memorial and research center in Jerusalem, established by law in 1953.

entries.title: Nobel Prize
entries.text: International prizes awarded since 1901. Israelis have won in chemistry, literature, economics and peace, among them Ada Yonath, S.Y. Agnon, Menachem Begin, Yitzhak Rabin, Shimon Peresand Daniel Kahneman.

entries.title: Eurovision Song Contest
entries.text: Annual European song contest. Netta Barzilai won it for Israel in 2018, and Israel has won four times.

entries.title: Technion
entries.text: Israel Institute of Technology in Haifa, founded in 1912 and opened in 1924.

entries.title: Negev
entries.text: Desert in the south that covers more than half of Israel's land. Its main city is Be’er Sheva, and the settlement of the Negev was a goal of David Ben-Gurion.

entries.title: Sea of Galilee
entries.text: Freshwater lake about 21 kilometers long, about 210 meters below sea level, and Israel's main reservoir. Many events of the life of Jesus took place on its shores.

entries.title: Iran
entries.text: Country east of Iraq, heir of the Persian Empire. It has been an Islamic republic since 1979 and backs Hezbollah and Hamas. The rankings in this book count it separately from the Arab League.

entries.title: Suez Crisis
entries.text: War of 1956 in which Israel, Britain and France attacked Egypt after it nationalized the Suez Canal. Israel took the Sinai and later withdrew.

entries.title: Nation-State Law
entries.text: Basic Law passed in 2018 that defines Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people.
